payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The cell has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to be suspended.
